clue.text: Scottish religious figure, male, adopting Mass by Sunday, after reflection

indicators.note: adopting means taking something in, so the male's letters take in the Mass abbreviation

parts.note: a stag is a male deer, so male stands for it

indicators.note: a reflection shows a thing back to front, so the word for Sunday is read backwards

explanation.surface: A description of a Scottish saint who, after some thought, takes up Sunday Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' and 'after reflection' are the two operations; 'by' only joins the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnus Erlendsson, Earl of Orkney, was canonised and is a patron saint venerated in Scotland.

clue.text: Is critical of flushing potassium in drains

indicators.note: flushing means driving out, so the potassium is expelled

parts.note: skewers means attacks or criticises sharply
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: Someone criticises the practice of pouring potassium down the drains.
explanation.definitionFit: Underground pipes carrying away waste water are the town's drainage system.

clue.text: Spy chief with cipher picked up in part of France

parts.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the word is lifted and read upwards

parts.note: a code is a cipher

explanation.surface: A spymaster's coded message is intercepted somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'picked up' reverses CODE to EDOC.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the wine-producing district of the Bordeaux region in south-west France.

clue.text: Craftiness will trap large number in place of execution

indicators.note: will trap means the craftiness word will close around the next pieces

parts.note: guile is cunning or craftiness
a lot is a large number

explanation.surface: Cunning will catch a crowd of victims at the scaffold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link word: it supplies its own letters, so LOTIN goes inside GUILE.
explanation.definitionFit: The blade machine stood where condemned people were beheaded, notably in revolutionary France.

clue.text: Persuades first son to leave waves

indicators.note: to leave means that letter is taken out of the waves

parts.note: surges are big waves

indicators.note: first means just the opening letter of son

explanation.surface: A father coaxes his eldest boy away from the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage someone strongly to act is to push or prompt them.

clue.text: One heading off into New York, location of 1's cathedral

indicators.note: into says the trimmed word goes inside the rearranged city
New suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of York
heading off means the first letter of the word One is cut away

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for New York, apparently in search of a cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads New York as one city; 'New' is really the anagram signal for York. '1' points to the answer at 1-across.
explanation.definitionFit: St Magnus Cathedral stands in Kirkwall, the main town of these islands off northern Scotland.

clue.text: Character provided by computer's fifth operation?

parts.note: a computer's run is one execution of a program
E is the fifth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A question about what a computer's fifth operation produces.
explanation.walkthrough: A computer's runs could be labelled A, B, C...: the fifth would be run E.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter of the ancient Germanic alphabet is one of its written characters.

clue.text: Brilliant playing — with energy — but losing line in tense moment

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with
losing means one line symbol is dropped from the letters of brilliant

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dazzling, energetic performance that falls flat at a key moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing line' drops an L from BRILLIANT to leave BRILIANT; add E and 'playing' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A gripping, suspenseful occasion is one that makes people chew their fingertips.

clue.text: County finally away from the crease, dismissing opener and conceding

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of County is taken
dismissing opener means the first letter is removed, with a cricket sense of getting an opening batter out

parts.note: in cricket the side that is not batting at the crease is fielding

explanation.surface: A cricket county, out in the field, loses its opening batter and gives way.
explanation.walkthrough: The crease is where the batter stands in cricket; the team away from it is fielding. 'dismissing opener' drops its F.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving way, submitting or surrendering is the same as giving ground.

clue.text: Slight shift of character in gardening work union

indicators.note: one letter, a character, moves a little, from E to the next letter of the alphabet, D

parts.note: weeding is a routine garden chore

explanation.surface: A gardener's work changes slightly to become a union.
explanation.walkthrough: The second E of WEEDING moves one place along the alphabet to D: a 'slight shift' of one character.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage ceremony joins two people in a union.

clue.text: Knight returning with another, coming in to go to court first thing

indicators.note: coming in means the knights' letters are placed within the word for going to court

parts.note: to sue is to go to court against someone
another knight, this time N, the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: returning means the knight's title together with the second knight is read backwards

parts.note: a knight is addressed as Sir

explanation.surface: Two knights arrive together at a royal court, one heading back.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the chess symbol for a knight, so 'another' knight is N; 'returning' turns both knights round together before 'coming in' places them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn, when the sun comes up, is the very start of the day, first thing in the morning.

clue.text: Oblique American supporting firm

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting piece sits below the one it holds up

parts.note: solid means firm

explanation.surface: An American backs a solid company.
explanation.walkthrough: The oblique is the slash mark (/), also called a stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: The printer's name for the slanting stroke used as a separator, the slash.

clue.text: Spots cunning in abandoning force without apparent thought

indicators.note: abandoning means the force symbol is left out of the spots

parts.note: freckles are small spots on the skin
F is the physics symbol for force
sly means cunning

explanation.surface: A cunning player gives up force and spots an opening, acting without thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops F from FRECKLES to leave RECKLES; 'in' joins on SLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting rashly, heedless of consequences, is acting with no visible forethought.

clue.text: A crook won't take closure of delicatessen lying down

indicators.note: won't take means the crook goes without one of its letters

parts.note: a crook is a bend, as in the crook of an arm

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its last letter, here of delicatessen

explanation.surface: A criminal refuses to accept the shutting of a deli lying down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closure of delicatessen' is N, which 'won't take' drops from BEND to leave BED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in bed is to be lying down, an old-fashioned adverb.

clue.text: It will guide ships around isle (though flickering)

indicators.note: flickering suggests the letters dancing about and rearranging, like a beam

explanation.surface: A beacon flickers but still guides ships around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flickering' rearranges ISLE plus THOUGH; the flicker is also apt for the light itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower with a bright lamp warns and guides vessels past dangerous coasts.

clue.text: Avoid old US educational establishment

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Advice to steer clear of a former American college.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something out is to skip or avoid it.

clue.text: Year mediating between market and cathedral — endless torment

indicators.note: mediating between means the year sits between the market and the cathedral

parts.note: a mart is a market
Dom is the German word for a cathedral, as in Kölner Dom

explanation.surface: A year spent going between market and cathedral, a lasting misery.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffering death or prolonged pain for one's beliefs, extended to any long agony.

clue.text: Not skilled and untested regarding sport

parts.note: bad at something means not skilled at it
mint condition means new, never used or tested
on means about or regarding

explanation.surface: A verdict on a novice player who has not yet been tried out at a game.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a racket game played with a shuttlecock over a high net.

clue.text: Old rail company carrying lightweight delivery

indicators.note: carrying means the rail company holds the light weight inside

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national rail company
an ounce is a small weight

explanation.surface: An old train operator transports a light parcel for delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a delivery is a ball bowled; this one rears up high at the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-pitched cricket ball that rises sharply is a particular kind of bowled ball.

clue.text: Artificial fuel unfortunately well below expectations?

parts.note: a sham is something fake or artificial

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters of fuel have gone wrong and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Synthetic fuel sadly turns out a disappointing failure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' is the anagram signal on fuel; the question mark flags the loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgraceful performance falls so far short of standards that it brings embarrassment.

clue.text: Hard debates about article prompting long speeches

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: about means the debating word goes around the article

parts.note: argues means debates
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Fierce arguments over a newspaper piece lead to lengthy oratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the article inside the debating word; 'prompting' just links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirades are long, ranting addresses, often aggressive in tone.

clue.text: Instrument tuned high, though not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter of the word for tuned high goes

parts.note: a note tuned a little high is sharp

explanation.surface: A musician's complaint about an instrument slightly out of tune.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a large stringed instrument plucked with the fingers.

clue.text: A very French finale from Bizet, not moving

parts.note: très is French for very

indicators.note: the finale from a word is its last letter, here of Bizet

explanation.surface: A very French ending from Bizet's opera closes on a still note.
explanation.definitionFit: Being motionless or still, like something settled and inactive.

clue.text: April 30, by implication, in Irish county

indicators.note: by implication says the date is only implied: the answer read as a date points back to it

parts.note: the day before May 1 would by that logic be May nought, with the nought read as the letter O

explanation.surface: A date at the end of April spent in a county of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by implication' marks the reverse logic: if May 1 follows April 30, then April 30 is in effect 'May nought', and the nought is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a county on the western Atlantic coast of Ireland, in Connacht.

clue.text: Phantom wreck overlooked for radio programme

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to wreck it

indicators.note: something put out on radio is only heard, so a word that sounds the same will do

parts.note: missed means overlooked

explanation.surface: A ghost ship's wreck passes unnoticed in the schedule for a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for radio programme' signals a sound-alike: MISSED is said like MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used for something imaginary or illusory that does not really exist.

clue.text: Discrimination some reject as terrible

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A discerning critic dismisses some things as awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Discernment in judging what is fine or fitting, as in a person of refined judgement.

clue.text: Keen on including right overture

indicators.note: including means the keen word takes the right symbol inside

parts.note: into means keen on, as in being into jazz

explanation.surface: An enthusiast keen on including just the right opening piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening passage leading into the main piece, the preliminary section.

clue.text: Pee, and pee endlessly — what's the excuse?

parts.note: the letter P sounds like the word pee, so P stands for it

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the second word is cut off

parts.note: to leak is slang for to urinate

explanation.surface: Someone demands to know why another person has wet themselves twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The same word does two jobs: first as the sound of a letter, then as a slang synonym trimmed by 'endlessly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An excuse or justification offered when called to account, as in a plea of mitigation.

clue.text: Crab last to scoff head from small fish

indicators.note: last to means the final letter of the following word, scoff
head from means the first letter of the small fish is removed

parts.note: a tiddler is a very small fish

explanation.surface: A crab is the last creature to wolf down the head of a small fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last to' and 'head from' both act on single letters; tiddler is British slang for a tiny fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The fiddler crab is a type of crab named for its one oversized claw.

clue.text: Bar story not mentioning a bus at the airport?

parts.note: to bar a door is to shut it

indicators.note: not mentioning means the letter A is left out of the story

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A tale from a bar in which nobody mentions the airport bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not mentioning' removes A from TALE to leave TLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An airport's shuttle service is a bus running to and fro between terminals or car parks.

clue.text: Priests welcoming millions for religious festival

indicators.note: welcoming means the priests take the millions in

parts.note: lamas are Tibetan Buddhist priests
M is the standard abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Clergy welcome vast crowds to a religious celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the harvest feast of 1 August, when loaves made from the new wheat were blessed.

clue.text: Sign of disaffection about ruined tree is to diminish

indicators.note: about means the sulky look goes around the other letters

parts.note: a pout shows sulky displeasure

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of tree are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sulks over a ruined tree, and their resentment fades.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' scrambles tree and 'about' wraps the sulk round it; 'is to' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to dwindle gradually and come to an end.
